transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-09
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Zhou (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (CTO - Tidepool Labs), Aisha Rahman (Platform Eng), Daniel Ortega (Head of Security)
Recording id: ff-20270909-tpl-8421

Summary:
- Tidepool Labs evaluating Redwood for a mix of Hosted + Private (VPC) deployment; primary concerns are network egress, KMS integration, and observability hooks for their gateway/proxy layer.
- Integration needs: LangChain and LlamaIndex connectors, an edge gateway (proxy) in front of Redwood for routing multi-tenant traffic, rate-limit/quota enforcement compatibility, and token-level cost visibility.
- Next steps agreed: share private deployment checklist, sample adapter code for LangChain/LlamaIndex, and schedule pilot kickoff with security and infra.

Topics:
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
- SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex support and adapters
- Gateway/proxy placement and egress requirements
- Rate limits/quotas and per-tenant observability
- Security: SOC2, KMS, SSO, audit logs

Action items (captured during call):
- Marcus: network diagram + egress policy (due 2027-09-16)
- Ethan: integration snippets for LangChain/LlamaIndex (due 2027-09-13)
- Samira: pricing ranges and pilot scope doc (due 2027-09-14)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samira (Redwood AE): All right, hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samira — I'm the AE on this. We have Ethan from the SE team with me. Marcus, Aisha, Daniel — thanks for taking the time. Is the time still good on your side?
[00:08] Marcus (Tidepool): Yep, good here. We had to shuffle a bit internally but all set.
[00:12] Aisha (Tidepool): Morning / afternoon — thanks.
[00:15] Ethan (Redwood SE): Hi all. Quick agenda: run through your goals, current infra, then dive into integration patterns — SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex, and the gateway/proxy questions. We'll surface Hosted/Dedicated/Private tradeoffs.
[00:27] Marcus: Sounds good. To set context — Tidepool builds a healthcare-ish SaaS that processes device telemetry and generates clinician summaries. We plan to embed an LLM feature for triage and summarization. Main constraints: PHI-like datapoints, strict egress policies, and we need per-tenant observability. Timeline: pilot in 2–3 weeks, production in Q4 if all goes well.
[00:46] Samira: Great. Quick clarifying Qs: do you need all inference on-prem, or is hybrid okay?
[00:51] Marcus: Hybrid ideally. We want most traffic in Hosted but anything with PII/PHI must live in our VPC or an on‑prem appliance. So Redwood Private (VPC or on‑prem) is attractive.
[01:02] Daniel: And from security side we need KMS/HSM integration for keys, SOC2 evidence, audit logs shipped to our SIEM, and SSO via SAML.
[01:10] Ethan: Totally expected. Redwood Private supports customer KMS and audit forwarding; we can outline the specifics. On the integration side, you mentioned LangChain and LlamaIndex — what are you using today?
[01:20] Aisha: Our app uses LangChain for orchestration and LlamaIndex for some retrieval-augmented steps. We currently have a gateway that routes to OpenAI and Anthropic endpoints. We'd like Redwood to fit into that pipeline with minimal code changes — ideally an adapter in our gateway.
[01:33] Samira: Good. So integration patterns: 1) direct SDK calls from your backend to Redwood Hosted for non‑PHI requests, 2) route PHI traffic to a Redwood Private instance in your VPC via a gateway/proxy, or 3) Dedicated pool for predictable throughput if you need committed capacity. All three are supported.
[01:48] Marcus: Can we put a gateway in our network that handles auth, rate limiting and then forwards to Redwood? We're trying to keep a single ingress.
[01:56] Ethan: Yes. Common pattern is to run a proxy (Envoy/nginx or our reference gateway) inside your VPC. It does tenant auth, rate limiting/quotas, and then talks to Redwood Private over a secured peering. The proxy can also forward KV cache prefixes if you want to reuse tokens — we call it KV cache but sometimes the transcriber writes KVcash or KV-cache, sorry if that pops up in docs.
[02:17] Aisha: How about the SDKs — will our LangChain/LlamaIndex code see big diffs? We don't want to rework prompt templates.
[02:22] Ethan: We provide a Python SDK and a drop‑in LangChain wrapper; LlamaIndex connectors are a small adapter. In many cases it's a 3‑5 line change — e.g., swap the endpoint and model name. We'll share a sample repository. There are a few gotchas: streaming semantics differ slightly under our batching runtime, and function calling behavior needs a small adapter to map tool names.
[02:41] Marcus: Streaming semantics — can you elaborate? We stream partial outputs to the UI. Latency is critical for interactive triage.
[02:47] Ethan: Redwood supports streaming in Hosted and Private. Under Dedicated it gets even better for p99 because of reserved GPUs. However, with aggressive batching you can see a small increase in tail latency unless you set strict latency SLOs on that route. We recommend configuring two routes: interactive (low batch, higher cost) and background (high batch, low cost). The routing is controlled via headers or route keys from your gateway.
[03:08] Daniel: Rate limiting — we already have per-tenant quotas. Does Redwood support quota tokens or headers we can use?
[03:12] Samira: Yes. We surface per-request metadata: tokens consumed, model, latency. For quotas you can set per-api-key limits on Hosted and per-tenant policies on Dedicated/Private. The recommended pattern when you front with a proxy is to pass an inline tenant id header and map that to Redwood API keys on the backend. That also gives you token-level billing info per tenant.
[03:33] Aisha: For observability we'd like to ingest traces into our OpenTelemetry pipeline and see token breakdowns. Is that available?
[03:39] Ethan: We ship tracing hooks — OpenTelemetry compatible. You can also export per-route token/latency metrics via our telemetry endpoint or push to Datadog/Prometheus. There is a small agent for Private deployments that forwards metrics to your endpoints. We'll send the observability integration doc.
[03:56] Marcus: Security question — zero trust? We need mTLS and private peering.
[03:59] Samira: For Private you can choose mTLS plus VPC peering or VPN; on‑prem appliances use HSM-backed keys. For Hosted we use strict controls but anything flagged as PHI should go to Private. We'll include the architecture options in the checklist.
[04:12] Daniel: On audit logs — can Redwood stream full request/response payloads to our SIEM, or is that something we keep local in the VPC?
[04:18] Ethan: For Private deployments you can configure log forwarding to a Syslog/HTTPS endpoint in your network. For Hosted we provide structured metadata and redaction options, but we don't forward raw PHI unless you have a private plan with an ingest agreement.
[04:33] Marcus: Ok. How does pricing look? We need ballpark for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for planning.
[04:38] Samira: I'll put together ranges — Hosted per-token pricing, Dedicated as committed monthly for GPU pools with overage, Private includes platform fee + deployment costs and optional support. I can send a sample TCO with an example of mixed routing (Hosted for non-sensitive, Private for PHI) — that usually helps customers.
[04:53] Aisha: A technical nit — we use LlamaIndex to persist indexes on s3 and then call the LLM for refine steps. Any restrictions on S3 endpoints or special network routes when calling Private?
[05:04] Ethan: If your index is in S3 within your VPC, you can mount a VPC endpoint and we can reach it if Private is deployed in the same VPC or via VPC peering. Otherwise, we recommend pulling the index into your gateway and only sending the embeddings or retrieval results to Redwood. Small latency difference but simpler security.
[05:20] Marcus: Does Redwood support custom models or bring-your-own-model? We have some tuned models internally that we may want to run on Dedicated.
[05:26] Ethan: Yes — Dedicated and Private support BYOM (bring your own model) if the model is containerized or in a supported format; there are constraints on CUDA/quantization depending on the hardware. We'll include the model onboarding checklist.
[05:36] Samira: Quick question — who are the decision stakeholders? Marcus: CTO and platform lead. Daniel handles security signoff. Pricing owner is me — product ops.
[05:45] Marcus: That's right. Also, procurement may want a PoC agreement for 30 days.
[05:50] Samira: We can do a pilot with limited seats — typical flow is 2 weeks of integration + 1 week of load tests.
[05:58] Aisha: For the pilot we need some concrete sample code.
[06:01] Ethan: I'll prepare LangChain and LlamaIndex adapter snippets and a small proxy config for Envoy that shows header mapping and rate-limit filters.
[06:09] Daniel: Can you also include the SOC2 report and a KMS integration guide so we can run it by our audit team?
[06:14] Samira: Yes — I'll attach our compliance pack.
[06:18] Marcus: On quotas again — does Redwood expose a webhook when a tenant reaches quota, or do we have to poll metrics?
[06:23] Ethan: There's both. You can set up quota policies with webhook callbacks for imminent limit and exceeded events, and we also provide push metrics.
[06:29] Aisha: One more thing — is there a recommended pattern for cache invalidation for KV cache (we want fresh summaries on new device data)?
[06:36] Ethan: Common approach: use a short TTL for device streams and tag cache keys with a timestamp or a sequence id. If you need strict consistency, route those calls to the Private instance with no caching.
[06:47] Marcus: This is helpful. Are there any red flags you normally see with healthcare customers?
[06:51] Samira: Biggest is unclear data flow — ensure you can segregate PHI before it leaves your VPC. Also, check retention settings for embeddings and whether you want to store them encrypted in your KMS.
[07:03] Daniel: For compliance we'll need a written data flow and retention policy before pilot.
[07:07] Samira: We'll include that in the pilot doc.
[07:12] Marcus: Cool. I have a question about function calling — we call specialist tools (scheduling, EHR lookups) via function calls. Any differences?
[07:20] Ethan: Function calling works across Hosted/Dedicated/Private; with Private you get more control over tool invocation and you can host the tool endpoints internal only. One caveat: if you use streaming + function calls you need to handle partial outputs; we'll provide guidelines.
[07:34] Aisha: Can you show an example of a LangChain chain that uses a Redwood endpoint?
[07:38] Ethan: Sure — quick high level: replace the llm object with RedwoodLLM wrapper in your chain, keep the prompt templates the same, and adjust the client config for model name and streaming callback. I'll send a gist.
[07:48] (brief cross-talk about scheduling)
[08:00] Samira: Let's recap next steps. Marcus, you'll share the network diagram and egress policy. Ethan will push integration snippets. I'll send pricing and compliance pack. We should aim to reconvene for pilot kickoff week of 2027-09-20.
[08:15] Marcus: That works. Also please include a short runbook for the Envoy proxy config — we use rate‑limit filters already, so a sample mapping to Redwood headers would be great.
[08:25] Ethan: Will do. I'll include a small Envoy config and an NGINX example.
[08:30] Daniel: One procedural note — procurement prefers a light MSA before we start if we're touching PHI. Samira, do you know your legal team's timelines?
[08:39] Samira: Yes, we can provide a PoC addendum and an MSA template. I'll ask legal and loop back.
[08:44] Marcus: OK. Anything else?
[08:46] Aisha: No — thanks.
[08:48] Samira: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule.

End of transcript.
